eligibility_text: ABOUT THE PROGRAM The Sousou Graduate Fellows Program (SGFP) supports exceptional Palestinian students pursuing master's or PhD studies at top-tier universities in the United States and the United Kingdom. It supports students who have received admission and a financial aid offer from an SGFP-eligible university but require additional support to cover the remaining funding gap and accept their offer. View the complete list of eligible universities HERE . SGFP PRIORITIZES Academic excellence Leadership potential Proven financial need Giving back to your local community ‎and homeland PROGRAM FUNDING AMOUNTS Up to $30,000 per year Master’s-level study Up to $20,000 per year PhD-level study UP TO 2 YEARS of scholarship support for eligible fellows SGFP awards are limited and are intended to cover the remaining tuition gap after university financial aid and all other available financial resources have been applied. ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS Hold a Palestinian, Jerusalem, or refugee ID, or demonstrate Palestinian descent. Demonstrate financial need and come from a low-income background. Have Fall 2027 admission and a financial-aid offer from an SGFP-eligible university in the U.S. or UK. Show academic excellence, leadership potential, and commitment to positive contributions to Palestine and beyond. Be eligible to obtain a student visa for the U.S. or the UK. APPLICATION REQUIREMENTS Please prepare the following documents before you start completing this application as you will have to upload copies of them before you are able to submit this online application. Official university admission letter and financial aid offer from the university. Report and documentation for any scholarships or financial awards received from organizations or institutions outside the university that will be used to support your intended studies. Copy of your passport (all). Copy of your Palestinian, Jerusalem, refugee ID card, or background demonstrating Palestinian descent. Supporting financial documents/proof of income (salary slip/letter of employment indicating your monthly or annual income). Bank statement to verify the information provided in your application regarding personal or family contributions toward the cost of your studies. Proof of any financial assistance or scholarship you received in previous educational levels. Proof of any other financial support that you/your family receive. APPLICATION PERIOD Opens: January 15, 2027 Closes: April 15, 2027 HOW TO APPLY The application will open on January 15, 2027. CONTACT INFORMATION Email: sgfp@amideast.org Tel: +970-2-2408023

eligibility_text: The application for the Fulbright Foreign Student Program in the West Bank is now closed. About the Program The Fulbright Program is the flagship international academic exchange program sponsored by the U.S. government. Led by the U.S. government in partnership with more than 160 countries worldwide, Fulbright offers life-changing international academic and cultural exchange opportunities to study, research, and contribute to finding solutions to complex global challenges.  Fulbright provides participants, who represent the best and brightest of U.S. society and of societies abroad, are chosen for their academic merit and leadership potential. The Fulbright Foreign Student Program supports graduate students, early career professionals, and researchers to research and study in the United States for one year or longer at U.S. universities or other educational institutions. Participants also experience life in the United States and share their culture and traditions with Americans. Participants will be selected through an open, merit-based competition in which leadership potential, academic excellence, and the ability to adjust to life in the United States are considered.  By receiving a Fulbright Foreign Student Program award, participants become part of a global network of Fulbright participants and alumni. The Fulbright Foreign Student Program is a program of the U.S. Department of State with funding provided by the U.S. Government and is administered by Amideast in the Middle East and North Africa region. Benefits Besides earning your master’s degree or pursuing graduate-level research at a U.S. university, there are many benefits of the Fulbright Program, including, but not limited to: Learning about the United States and engaging American culture and sharing your own culture and traditions. Enriching your knowledge and improving employment prospects with a graduate degree or graduate level research. Joining a global Fulbright community and finding solutions to complex global challenges. Contributing to professional developemnt and research at U.S. universities. Collaborate with U.S. host institutions and businesses. Covered award costs include tuition, a living allowance, and round-trip travel. Applicant Requirements The Fulbright Foreign Student Program is for graduates and professionals from a variety of academic and professional backgrounds.  A competitive applicant should have an excellent academic record, strong English language skills, and the commitment to return to their country or territory of nomination upon completion of the Program. The requirements to apply for the Fulbright Foreign Student Program are: Applicants must be Palestinian residents of Jerusalem or the West Bank who are eligible for a Palestinian Authority passport or laiss

eligibility_text: The Hope Fund program enables underserved Palestinian youth, many from refugee backgrounds, to benefit from an undergraduate education in the United States. The program provides grants (financial assistance) to promising, academically qualified but financially challenged students from Gaza, the West Bank, and Jerusalem, to assist them in pursuing their undergraduate studies at U.S. universities based in the United States or the MENA region. PROGRAM COMPONENTS This program provides financial assistance to students who were successful in securing undergraduate admission and substantial financial aid packages from a U.S. based university or U.S. university in the MENA region for Fall 2026 , but who are unable to accept the offer without additional financial assistance. If eligible, The Hope Fund program would cover additional supplemental costs like books, supplies, health insurance, travel expenses (i.e., expenses beyond the basics of most university scholarships, such as tuition and room and board). Applications are accepted on a rolling basis until June 20, 2026 , as long as funds are available. Amideast will evaluate applications as they are received. Eligibility Requirements The Hope Fund seeks applicants who: Come from a low-income background. Candidates residing in a refugee camp will be given priority; Secured admission and a substantial financial aid package from a U.S. based university or U.S. university in the MENA region to start their undergraduate program in Fall 2026; The financial aid package from the university must cover at least 80% of the total university’s cost of attendance; Currently in the 12th grade or completed 12th grade in 2025 at a school in the West Bank, Jerusalem, or Gaza; Current legal resident in the West Bank, Jerusalem, or Gaza; must be a resident throughout the entire candidacy process to be eligible. Gazan applicants currently outside of Gaza should contact Amideast to confirm eligibility.; Able to obtain a U.S. student visa; American citizens and/or U.S. Green Card holders are not eligible. How to apply Application closed on June 20, 2026. For additional information, please contact Amideast: West Bank applicants: 02-240-8023 ext. 111 Gaza applicants: 02-240-8023 ext. 106 Email Address: WestBank@amideast.org

eligibility_text:
Promoting peace is one of Rotary’s main causes. The fully funded Rotary Peace Fellowship, which covers tuition and living expenses, increases the capacity of existing leaders to prevent and resolve conflict by offering academic training, field experience, and professional networking. 

Up to 130 fellows are selected every year in a globally competitive process based on personal, academic, and professional achievements. Fellows earn either a master’s degree or a professional development certificate in peace and development studies at one of the seven Rotary Peace Centers, located at leading universities around the world.  
 
More than 1,300 program alumni are working in more than 115 countries as leaders in national governments, nongovernmental organizations, social enterprises, the military, law enforcement, and international organizations such as the United Nations. 
 
Master’s degree  
- 15-24 month program, small-group classroom learning, in fields related to peace and development 
- Intended for leaders near the start of their careers 
- 50 fellows selected annually to study at one of five Rotary Peace Centers at partner universities, which offer interdisciplinary curricula with research-informed teaching 
- 2-3 month field study experience to develop practical skills 
- Fellows connect with an international cohort of fellows, thought leaders, and a global network of Rotarians 
 
Professional development certificate 
- Yearlong program that blends online learning, in-person classes, and an independent project, based at a Rotary Peace Center in Thailand or Uganda 
- Intended for social change leaders with extensive experience working in peace-related fields
- 80 fellows selected annually to earn a certificate in peace and development studies 
- Interdisciplinary program includes a two-week online preliminary course, 10 weeks of on-site courses with field studies, a nine-month period during which fellows implement a social change initiative (with interactive online sessions), and an on-site capstone seminar 

Eligibility: Take the eligibility quiz online. See link below. 
 
Qualified candidates must:   
- Have three years of related work experience for the master’s program 
- Have five years of related work experience for the certificate program and be able to explain how their plan to promote peace aligns with Rotary’s mission  
- Be proficient in English
- Have a bachelor’s degree  
- Demonstrate leadership skills 
- Have a strong commitment to cross-cultural understanding and peace 

Applications need to be submitted to Rotary districts by 31 May. Please write to the email address below with questions. (Registered users can see contact details).
Peace fellowship applicants must meet these requirements:

Proficiency in English; a second language is strongly recommended
Demonstrated commitment to international understanding and peace 
Excellent leadership skills
Master’s degree applicants: minimum three years

As an international shipping company that gives communities around the globe access to U.S. goods, MyUS.com understands the power of connection. By connecting teachers to educational supplies for their classrooms, medical professionals to the latest innovations in healthcare, and countless others to resources they couldn’t otherwise access, MyUS.com helps customers shape the world around them.

This power of community can’t be understated - particularly for students working hard to achieve their educational goals and find their place in the world. Because connecting to one’s community is such an integral part of Ramadan observances, MyUS.com is interested in understanding how your community has affected the way you approach your studies and your future career.

Ramadan is a time of spiritual reflection, devotion and connecting with family and community. It’s also a time to give back. And that’s why we are excited to announce the MyUS.com Community Scholarship, a global annual scholarship that will provide select eligible students with financial assistance as they earn their degrees.

To qualify for scholarship consideration, eligible students should write a 500-word essay detailing how self-reflection, introspection and community outreach have affected their choices in life, including what to study, which university/college to attend and which career they will pursue after graduation.
How to Apply:
To enter, visit the website or send an email with the following information:

Your essay (attached as a document or included in the body of the email)
A photo of yourself (image must feature you alone, without other people)
Any additional relevant information you feel will help tell your story
Any submissions not received through this email will be disqualified. If you’re having trouble submitting your essay, please contact us for assistance.

Essays will be reviewed - and the recipient will be selected - based on the student’s ability to communicate their story as it relates to the questions above and to the overarching theme of the scholarship, as well as the thoughtfulness of their essay.

Below, you’ll find a number of questions that may help you in crafting your essay:
How specifically did you connect with your community during Ramadan?
What three lessons did you learn as a result of these connections, and how do you anticipate they will help you in the future?
How can you continue to connect with your community after Ramadan?
In what ways do you believe you will change the way you approach your studies after connecting with your community?
Do you have any advice for others who want to connect with their community?
How do you plan to be involved in your community after graduation?

Eligibility:
To apply for the scholarship, the applicant must be a student currently enrolled at an officially recognized, accredited college or university. Students who are not currently enrolled but have been accepted to attend may be eligible

eligibility_text:
Creating opportunities that can change lives, we established the British Council IELTS Award in order to assist high calibre individuals who have a strong motivation to develop their career and who can demonstrate that they have the potential to contribute to society with their studies.

The award will enable successful applicants to study at an undergraduate or postgraduate level at an institution of higher education anywhere in the world (in Germany or abroad), in an English taught program that accepts IELTS as part of its admission requirements.

The British Council IELTS Award is worth between £3,000 up to £10,000 depending on the tuition fees of the institution chosen by the winner and will go towards the cost of tuition fees of the individual's selected course.

If tuition fees of the successful candidate are below the maximum individual award fund of £10,000, remaining funds may be allocated to support other runners-up.  

The successful applicant will demonstrate a commitment to networking within the IELTS community and sharing their experience with other IELTS candidates.
To be eligible to apply for the British Council IELTS Award Germany you must:

- be aged 18 years 
- have taken an IELTS test at a British Council centre in Germany and received an official Test Report Form (TRF) dated between 1 June 2021 and 30 June 2022 issued by the British Council in Germany
- have achieved a minimum overall band score of 6.5, plus a minimum score of 6.5 in each of the four components of the IELTS test
- be planning to enrol on a full-time undergraduate or postgraduate programme taught in English at a university or other institution of higher education in Germany or abroad, which accepts IELTS as part of its admission requirements (check the official recognition list.). The tuition fees of the programme of choice must be a minimum of £3,000.
- be able to provide an acceptance letter from the relevant educational organisation .

The documents to be sent digitally for the first selection are:

2) Curriculum;
3) Copy of the doctoral thesis;
4) Copy of publications.

Program Overview
Leading a nonprofit organization is a rewarding task that requires in-depth knowledge and practical skills. Hebrew University’s MA in Nonprofit Management and Leadership provides students with the foundations of nonprofit organizational development and management, drawing on the vast expertise of Israel’s most established Faculty of Social Work. 

The core and elective courses in the program cover organizational, social, and financial aspects of nonprofit management and leadership. Students learn about leadership models, social policy and entrepreneurship, community organizing, philanthropy, and more.

The program is three semesters long and runs from October through September. During the autumn and spring semesters, students attend courses two full days a week. During the summer semester, they participate in four weeks of marathon courses (seven hours a day, four days a week, with each course lasting one week). Students also partake in a supervised team project and collaborate with a nonprofit organization during their year of study.
Eligibility
To be eligible for acceptance, you must have the following:
•	Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution of higher education recognized by the Hebrew University
•	Minimum B average (85/100 or equivalent)
•	Demonstrated knowledge of English

In addition to your online application, you will be required to submit the following documents:
•	Academic Records: Applicants must submit transcripts and diplomas from all prior academic degrees.
•	Proof of English Proficiency: A TOEFL exam score of 80 or above, IELTS exam score of 6 or above, or Amiram exam score of 120 or above. **
•	A CV and Statement of Purpose
•	Two Academic Recommendations
•	Photocopy of your Passport ID page
•	A Medical Form and Disclaimer Form (the latter for US citizens only) – both forms may be downloaded from the application website.

** If you have completed a degree at a university at which English is the sole language of instruction, or if you have completed a degree in English Language and Literature, you can request an exemption. You must submit documentation from your university verifying English as the language of instruction. Exemption is not automatic and is determined on a case-by-case basis.

Application Process
Applicants who have submitted applications will receive an email from the Graduate Office within about three business days, confirming receipt of their application and providing information on how to submit the supplementary application documents. Once applicants submit all of the required supplementary documents, their files will be sent to our Admission Committee for review, and they can expect to receive an admission decision – via email – within about ten days.

- Access to library resources.
- Access to IT services.

For the current Marie Sklodowska-Curie Postdoctoral Fellowships call, Sacro Cuore Don Calabria Hospital is pleased to support excellent researcher who are interested in submitting an application for the Marie Sklodowska-Curie Postdoctoral Fellowship call in the area of:
1.	Parasitology, with main focus on schistosomiasis and strongyloidiasis, both in the non-endemic setting (migrants’ and travellers’ health) and in endemic areas (infield collaborations
2.	Emerging/re-emerging viral infections, mainly arboviral infections, both in the non-endemic setting (migrants’ and travellers’ health) and in endemic areas (infield collaborations)

The Department of Infectious, Tropical Diseases and Microbiology of the IRCCS Sacro Cuore Don Calabria Hospital offers a truly international and multi-disciplinary workplace. Thanks to a world-wide research network you will be involved in a continuous fruitful exchange of experiences.

Who are we?

The Department of Infectious, Tropical Diseases and Microbiology is a referral centre for parasitic diseases In Italy. It is a WHO collaborating centre for strongyloidiasis and other Neglected Tropical Diseases. The Department comprises in and outpatient services and a diagnostic area. Translational research in the infectious disease field is carried out, mainly concerning parasitology, virology and emerging pathogens. Also, collaborations with low and middle income countries are ongoing, with infield activities. Cutting-edge equipment for molecular and cellular biology, immunoassays, protein analyses and BSL2/BLS3 cell culture are available.

1.	The researcher must be in possession of a doctoral degree or have successfully defended their doctoral thesis before call deadline to the European Commission (11/09/2024)

3.	The researcher can be of any nationality and must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Italy for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately before the call deadline (11/09/2024).

Application 
Candidates interested in this position should submit their Expression of Interest application at the email address below any time before 30/06/2024 (internal deadline), sending:

1.	a detailed curriculum vitae, including the list of publications;
2.	A motivation letter;
3.	Brief 1-page proposal of your future research project

The selected candidates will be supported in the development of their project proposals that must be submitted to the European Commission by September 11th, 2024 - h. 17.00 CET.

The Zukunftskolleg is an Institute for Advanced Study (IAS). It offers fellowships as well as a diverse support network to promote the independence of early career researchers. Researchers at the postdoctoral level can work with minimal administrative constraints, and enjoy the freedom to engage in meaningful exchange with other up-and-coming colleagues as well as with distinguished senior researchers. Researchers in the humanities, social and natural sciences come to Konstanz from around the world to perform first-class research. The Zukunftskolleg is a keystone in the University of Konstanz's institutional strategy and the University of Konstanz is one of Germany’s eleven Universities of Excellence.

The foundation “Manfred Ulmer-Stiftung für Wissenschaft und Gesellschaft” at the University of Konstanz will be funding one of the fellowships. The "Centre for the Advanced Study of Collective Behaviour" and the Cluster of Excellence “The Politics of Inequality” will fund up to two fellowships for related projects in one of their interdisciplinary research fields. Free applications are encouraged (Track A – up to 4 scholarships) but also upon nomination (Track B – up to 4 scholarships).

Up to 8 (post-)doctoral stipends for an on-campus research stay at the Zukunftskolleg are available for 3 months (with justification for up to 4 months). The on-site ZUKOnnect Fellowships are complemented by a digital affiliation extending it to a duration of 12-months. The start date for the digital affiliation is 1. August 2025. The preferred start date for the on-site ZUKOnnect Fellowships is 1. October 2025.

title: Oxford Pershing Square Graduate Scholarships
provider: Pershing Square Foundation/ University of Oxford
description:
The Pershing Square Foundation funds full scholarships for outstanding students on Oxford’s 1+1 MBA, which combines a one-year Master’s degree at the University of Oxford with the one-year Oxford MBA. The scholarships are for people who want to tackle major social challenges.
•  full course fees for both the Master’s degree and the MBA; •  a grant for living costs of at least £21,805 for each year of study; •  mentoring, conferences and events with the Pershing Square Scholar community.
eligibility_text:
Applicants from any country
Applicants must apply to the Oxford 1+1 MBA and meet the entry requirements of both the Oxford MBA and their chosen Master’s programme. Selection is based on leadership potential, academic achievement, personal character and integrity, and the applicant’s vision for using the 1+1 MBA to tackle a major challenge.
You must make two separate applications: one to your chosen Master’s programme by its own deadline (December 2026 or January 2027, depending on the course), and one to the 1+1 MBA by 6 January 2027 . In the Funding section of the 1+1 MBA application, upload an essay of no more than 500 words answering: ‘How do you intend to change the world and what does this tell us about you as a person?’ It is important to visit the official website (link found below) for detailed information on how to apply for this scholarship.

title: EPFL Excellence Fellowships for Bachelor’s and Master’s Students
description:
École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL) offers a limited number of Excellence Fellowships at Bachelor’s and Master’s level to the most deserving students, chosen on academic excellence, qualifications and motivation. Some fellowships are funded by EPFL and others through partnerships with foundations and companies.
The Master Excellence Fellowship pays CHF 10,000 per semester for up to four semesters (three for a 90-credit Master’s), and external candidates also get a reserved room in a student residence. Tuition fees and rent are not included, so fellows pay these from the fellowship or other funds. To keep the fellowship in the second year, you must earn the required credits with a high grade average. The Bachelor Excellence Fellowship is spread over the three years of the Bachelor’s.
eligibility_text:
Students of any nationality, including international students
The Master Excellence Fellowships are for outstanding students starting a Master’s programme at EPFL. Applicants who already hold a Master’s degree or are already enrolled in an EPFL Master’s are not eligible, and you can apply for only one Master’s programme a year. The Bachelor fellowships are for final-year high school students with remarkable school and extracurricular results.
For the Master Excellence Fellowship, apply through EPFL’s online Master’s application and tick the box asking to be considered for an Excellence Fellowship. Only applications that are paid for and validated by 15 December 2026 are considered for the fellowship; applications validated after that date (for example, in the 31 March 2027 admission round) are reviewed for admission only. Recommendation letters are due by 31 January 2027. EPFL Bachelor’s students continuing to a Master’s in the same field follow a separate procedure through their section. For the Bachelor Excellence Fellowship, tick the box on your Bachelor’s application form and send the requested file by the date shown on the official website. It is important to read the fellowship guidelines and visit the official websites (links found below) for detailed information on how to apply.

title: Gates Cambridge Scholarships for International Students
description:
The Gates Cambridge Scholarships are one of the most prestigious international scholarships in the world. Scholarships are awarded to outstanding applicants from countries outside the UK to pursue a full-time postgraduate degree in any subject available at the University of Cambridge.
A Gates Cambridge Scholarship covers the full cost of studying at Cambridge including tuition fees, maintenance allowance (£23,152 for 12 months at the 2026-27 rate; pro rata for courses shorter than 12 months) – for PhD scholars the award is for up to 4 years), one economy single airfare at both the beginning and end of the course and inbound visa costs & the cost of the Immigration Health Surcharge. It also provides additional, discretionary funding such as academic development funding, family allowance, fieldwork, etc. Read about the full scholarship value at this link .
eligibility_text:
Citizens of any country outside the United Kingdom.
You can apply for a Gates Cambridge Scholarship if you are: •  a citizen of any country outside the United Kingdom. •  applying to pursue one of the following full-time residential courses of study: PhD (full-time or part-time*), MSc or MLitt (full-time), or a one year postgraduate course (full-time) with some exceptions (see list above).
You must apply for admission and funding through the University’s Graduate Application Portal, and complete the Gates Cambridge part of the funding section. There are two Gates Cambridge application deadlines: 14 October 2026 (for US citizens resident in the USA) and either 8 December 2026 or 6 January 2027 depending on the course (for all other eligible applicants). It is important to read the How to Apply section and visit the official website (link found below) for detailed information on how to apply for this scholarship.

title: University of Sydney International Stipend Scholarship (USYDIS)
description:
The University of Sydney International Stipend Scholarship (USYDIS) is funded by the University of Sydney for high-quality international students doing a research Master’s or PhD. Students who receive it are also given the University of Sydney International Tuition Fee Scholarship, so their tuition is fully covered. The same application also considers international students for the Australian Government RTP scholarships.
•  a living stipend of AUD 44,293 a year (2027 rate) •  relocation and thesis allowances •  100% of tuition fees through the University of Sydney International Tuition Fee Scholarship Support lasts for up to 14 research periods (full-time) for a PhD, or up to 7 research periods for a research Master’s.
eligibility_text:
International students
You must: •  be a commencing or enrolled international student; •  have an outstanding record of academic achievement and research potential; •  have an unconditional offer for, or be enrolled in, a research Master’s or PhD at the University of Sydney.
Apply for admission to a research degree through Sydney Courses with all documents, and submit the scholarship application form by the deadline for your start date: •  Research periods 3 and 4, 2027 (second half of 2027): 18 December 2026 ; outcomes from 26 February 2027 •  Research periods 1 and 2, 2028: 10 September 2027 ; outcomes from 16 November 2027 It is important to visit the official website (link found below) for detailed information on how to apply for this scholarship.

title: Oxford-Weidenfeld and Hoffmann Scholarship and Leadership Programme
description:
The Oxford-Weidenfeld and Hoffmann Scholarships and Leadership Programme gives fully funded graduate scholarships at the University of Oxford to outstanding graduates and professionals from developing and emerging economies. Alongside their degree, scholars take part in a programme of leadership development, long-term mentoring and networking run by the Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Trust. The programme was set up in 2015, and the Trust also runs partnership schemes with Chevening and the Oxford Pakistan Programme.
100% of course fees and a grant for living costs of at least £21,805, for the full length of your fee liability on the agreed course. Scholars also join the Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Leadership Programme.

title: President’s PhD Scholarships at Imperial College London
description:
The President’s PhD Scholarships give high-achieving undergraduate and Master’s students the chance to do a fully funded PhD at Imperial College London. Around 50 scholars a year choose their own research project with the support of a leading supervisor and join a cohort of other President’s PhD Scholars.
Each scholarship provides the following for 3.5 years of PhD study: •  full tuition fees •  a stipend of £27,036 a year (2027-28 rate) to help with living costs •  a consumables fund of £2,000 a year for the first three years •  a programme of opportunities and events run by the Early Career Researcher Institute
eligibility_text:
Applicants of any nationality (Home or Overseas fee status).
To be considered, you should: •  hold, or expect to receive, a first-class undergraduate or integrated Master’s degree, or a distinction in a standalone Master’s degree (or the international equivalent); •  apply for a new PhD place at Imperial (current Imperial PhD students cannot apply); •  start your PhD between 1 August and 1 November 2027.
There is no separate scholarship form. Apply for a PhD through Imperial’s online application system and select the President’s PhD Scholarship option in the funding section. There are three rounds for 2027-28 entry: apply by 2 November 2026 (decisions by 31 January 2027), 11 January 2027 (decisions by 15 April 2027) or 1 March 2027 (decisions by 31 May 2027). Some departments run their own shortlisting first, so check your department’s page as well. It is important to visit the official website (link found below) for detailed information on how to apply for this scholarship.

title: Stockholm University Scholarships for International Students
description:
The Stockholm University Scholarship Scheme is for especially qualified students from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland who have to pay tuition fees. It covers the whole tuition fee for a Master’s programme at Stockholm University. Students apply for their Master’s programme first, and admitted students are then invited to apply for the scholarship.
The scholarship covers the whole tuition fee for your Master’s programme. It does not include living costs, so you will need to pay these yourself. Scholarship holders get priority for student housing through the university’s Housing Office.
eligibility_text:
Citizens of countries outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland who are required to pay tuition fees
To be eligible, you must: • be a citizen of a country outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland and be required to pay tuition fees; • be admitted to a Master’s programme at Stockholm University in the first (international) admission round. Scholarships are awarded on academic merit, and priority goes to applicants who rank Stockholm University as their first choice on universityadmissions.se.
Apply for your Master’s programme in the first (international) admission round on universityadmissions.se, which runs from 16 October 2026 to 15 January 2027 (admission deadline). Pay the application fee and send your documents by 1 February 2027, and rank Stockholm University as your first choice. Master’s admission results are published on 1 April 2027. Eligible students then receive the scholarship application form by email at the address in their University Admissions account. The 2027 scholarship deadline has not been announced yet. In the last round, the scholarship deadline was 30 March 2026 , just four days after admission results, so apply as soon as the form arrives. Scholarship results are announced by the end of April. It is important to visit the official website (link found below) for detailed information on how to apply for this scholarship.

title: Danish State Scholarships at University of Copenhagen
description:
The University of Copenhagen (UCPH), Denmark’s oldest and largest university, offers a limited number of tuition fee waivers and grants through the Danish Government Scholarship programme to highly talented students from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland. The scholarships are awarded only on academic achievement; financial need is not taken into account.
•  a full or partial tuition fee waiver; and/or •  an amount that covers basic living costs. What you receive depends on the faculty. At Health and Medical Sciences the scholarship covers tuition and living costs, or tuition only. At Science it covers tuition, and in exceptional cases living costs too, for the qualified applicants with the highest grades. At Theology it is a partial tuition fee waiver only. Grants for living costs are taxed in Denmark, although some nationalities are exempt.
eligibility_text:
Citizens of countries outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland
You must: •  be a citizen of a country outside the EU, the EEA and Switzerland; •  be admitted to a Master’s programme at the University of Copenhagen; •  be granted a time-limited residence permit to study in Denmark. You cannot receive the scholarship if you have the same legal rights as Danish citizens or qualify for the Danish State Educational Grant (SU). At the Faculty of Science, only applicants with a Bachelor’s grade average above 85% are considered.
You do not apply for the scholarship: all eligible non-EU/EEA applicants are considered automatically. Apply for admission to your Master’s programme through the university’s application portal between 15 November 2026 and 15 January 2027 (23:59 CET). Non-EU applicants pay an application deposit of DKK 1,120 (about EUR 150), which is not refunded if you are awarded a tuition fee waiver. The university contacts nominated applicants through the application portal. It is important to visit the official website (link found below) for detailed information on how to apply for this scholarship.

title: Maastricht University NL-High Potential Scholarships for International Students
description:
The Maastricht University (UM) NL-High Potential Scholarship programme offers full scholarships, including a tuition fee waiver and a monthly stipend, to highly talented students from outside the EU who have applied for a participating Master’s programme at UM. It combines the UM High Potential Scholarship, funded by the Maastricht University Scholarship Fund, with the national NL Scholarship. It is very competitive: only about 2% of applicants receive it.
The scholarship covers living expenses (€20,150 for 13 months or €38,750 for 25 months), health and liability insurance (€700), visa costs, the tuition fee and the pre-academic training. It lasts for the length of the Master’s: 13 months for a one-year programme and 25 months for a two-year programme.
eligibility_text:
Students with a nationality from outside the EU/EEA
Applicants must: •  hold a nationality from outside the EU/EEA, Switzerland and Suriname (and no EU/EEA dual nationality) and meet the Dutch visa and residence permit requirements; •  have applied for a participating full-time Master’s programme at UM for 2027-2028 and meet its admission requirements; •  never have taken part in a degree programme, or primary or secondary education, in the Netherlands (exchange students can apply); •  be no older than 35 on 1 September 2027; •  have excellent results, with a GPA of at least 7.5 out of 10 or equivalent; •  agree to act as a UM ambassador during and after their studies. Preference goes to candidates who do not already have a Master’s degree, and you can apply for only one UM scholarship.
First apply for a participating Master’s programme through Studielink and complete your admission application by 10 December 2026 . With your UM student number, fill in the scholarship application form online and upload the required documents between 1 October 2026 and 1 February 2027 (23:59 CET) . Documents cannot be added or replaced after you submit. It is important to visit the official website (link found below) for detailed information on how to apply for this scholarship.

title: Karsh International Scholarships at Duke University
description:
The Karsh International Scholarship was founded in 2010 through a gift from Martha L. and Bruce A. Karsh. It brings together an intellectually and civically engaged group of international students at Duke University who promote interdisciplinary inquiry, research and scholarship in the service of society. Applicants must have demonstrated financial need.
The scholarship covers four years of: •  tuition (US$73,740 in 2026-27), room and board, and mandatory fees •  any demonstrated need beyond those costs •  three summers of funding for research, unpaid internships and other opportunities
eligibility_text:
International students with financial need
Applicants should: •  be international students (not US citizens or permanent residents); •  be applying as first-year students (there is no aid for international transfer students); •  have strong academic preparation and documented financial need; •  tick the financial aid box on the Duke application, as international students who apply without aid cannot ask for it later.
There is no separate application and no nomination. Apply to Duke through the Common Application and apply for financial aid with the CSS Profile. The Early Decision deadline for 2027 entry was 2 November 2026; the Regular Decision deadline is 4 January 2027 , with financial aid forms due 1 February 2027. Duke is test-optional for this cycle. Finalists for merit scholarships are contacted in the spring and interviewed. It is important to visit the official website (link found below) for detailed information on how to apply for this scholarship.

title: Politecnico di Milano Merit-Based International Scholarships
description:
Politecnico di Milano (PoliMi) offers Merit-Based International Scholarships to the most talented international students starting a Master of Science programme taught in English. For 2027-28 there are 64 scholarships at the Milan campuses and the Piacenza, Cremona, Lecco and Mantova campuses.
All scholarships include a tuition fee waiver for the academic year, and scholarship holders pay only an administrative fee of about €190. In addition: •  Platinum: €10,000 gross, paid in two instalments; •  Gold: €8,000 gross, paid in two instalments; •  Gold Piacenza: €5,000 gross, paid in two instalments; •  Bronze Piacenza: €2,500 gross, paid at the start of the semester; •  Silver: tuition fee waiver only. The scholarship can be renewed for the second year (2028-29) if the student stays in the same MSc and reaches the required score from exam grades weighted by credits by 10 August 2028 (1,000 points for Platinum and 700 for Gold, Bronze and Silver). It cannot be combined with other scholarsh
eligibility_text:
International students
To be considered, you must: •  be an international student applying to the first year of a Master of Science taught in English for 2027-28; •  have submitted your MSc admission application and paid the application fee between 1 October and 1 December 2026; •  be admitted, accept the admission outcome and upload a valid English language certificate on the admission platform. Selection is based on merit, together with geographic origin, gender balance and age, and priority goes to candidates from countries that have suffered military aggression or are affected by civil war.
Submit the scholarship application through Politecnico di Milano Online Services (Benefits and Agreements > Economic benefits > Scholarships for International Master of Science Students a.y. 2027-2028) from 1 October 2026 until 12:00 noon (Italian time) on 15 December 2026 . No other method of application is accepted. A valid English language certificate must be submitted by 4 March 2027 to be considered, and results are emailed three to four months after the deadline. It is important to read the 2027-2028 Call for Applications and visit the official website (link found below) for detailed information on how to apply for this scholarship.

title: KU Leuven Inspiring the Outstanding Scholarship for International Students
description:
KU Leuven, Belgium’s largest university, offers the Inspiring the Outstanding Scholarship to an outstanding student from anywhere in the world who wants to take a Master’s or advanced Master’s programme. Paid for by the KU Leuven International Scholarship Fund, it is a full scholarship: the tuition fee is waived and the scholar receives a yearly allowance. The same application also puts students in the running for KU Leuven’s regional scholarships for Africa, ASEAN countries and Central and South America, and for the Flemish Government’s Master Mind Scholarships.
•  a full tuition fee waiver (scholars pay only an annual administration fee of about €140); •  a scholarship of €13,200 per academic year. The scholarship runs for one academic year for a 60 ECTS Master’s programme and two academic years for a 120 ECTS Master’s programme. By comparison, the KU Leuven Scholarship for Africa gives a full tuition fee waiver plus €4,000 for the whole programme.
eligibility_text:
International students from all countries. The regional scholarships are for nationals of the eligible countries in Africa, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America.
Applicants must: •  apply for an eligible Master’s or advanced Master’s programme at KU Leuven for 2027-2028; •  have an outstanding academic record; •  show a good command of English if English is not their first language, with a language test taken before 15 January 2027 (results can be added later); students who completed an English-taught programme in Australia, English-speaking Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, the United Kingdom or the United States do not need a certificate; •  not already be enrolled at a higher education institution in Flanders. The selection looks at academic performance and awards, motivation, relevant experience, leadership, commitment and the applicant’s overall profile. The scholarship is highly competitive.
There are two steps, both to be completed by 15 January 2027 (23:59 CET): •  submit a complete application for an eligible Master’s programme through the KU Leuven application tool, with the KU Leuven Scholarships & Master Mind Candidacy Form uploaded as an annexe; •  register your scholarship candidacy in the online registration tool. The Master’s programmes then nominate candidates, who are told by 10 March 2027 and asked to send a one-minute motivational video by 16 March 2027. A central KU Leuven committee makes the final selection, and results are expected at the end of March 2027. It is important to visit the official website (link found below) for the list of eligible programmes and detailed information on how to apply for this scholarship.

The Mastercard Foundation AfOx Graduate Scholarships fund talented Africans to study the one-year Oxford MBA at Saïd Business School. •  full MBA course fees; •  a grant for living costs of at least £21,805; •  tailor-made training, networking opportunities and support before, during and after your time at Oxford.

Citizens of African countries who normally live in Africa

There is no separate scholarship application. Submit your Oxford MBA application by 6 January 2027 and you will be considered automatically. title: Nanyang President’s Graduate Scholarship (NPGS) at NTU Singapore
description:
The Nanyang President’s Graduate Scholarship (NPGS) is a competitive and prestigious scholarship for outstanding graduates and final-year students who want to start a research career through a full-time PhD at Nanyang Technological University (NTU), one of Asia’s leading research universities. Students of all nationalities can apply.
The scholarship covers: •  the annual tuition fee; •  a monthly stipend of S$4,300 for international students (S$5,300 for Singapore citizens and S$4,800 for permanent residents); •  an overseas conference allowance of up to S$5,000 per financial year; •  a book allowance of S$500 a year; •  a one-time IT allowance of S$1,500; •  a one-time thesis allowance of S$600; •  priority for campus housing. The award is given for one year at first and renewed on good progress, for up to four years. There is no bond. International scholars must do teaching or laboratory supervision duties under NTU’s Graduate Assistantship Programme.
eligibility_text:
Students of all nationalities. NIE’s page notes that preference is given to Singapore citizens and permanent residents.
Applicants must have an Honours (Highest Distinction) degree or equivalent at Bachelor’s level. Final-year students must provide official documents from their university confirming that they are on track to graduate with Honours (Highest Distinction) or equivalent. Selection is by nomination only, and shortlisted candidates are interviewed.
Apply through NTU’s graduate admissions portal between 1 November 2026 and 31 December 2026 for Academic Year 2027-28. Applicants to NIE programmes apply between 2 November and 30 December 2026 through NIE’s own graduate application portal. You will need your identity documents, your degree certificates and transcripts (in the original language with an official English translation), a research proposal, two referee reports, a CV, any research publications, and test scores (IELTS, TOEFL, GRE, GMAT or GATE) where required. Results and admission offers are sent by email. It is important to visit the official website (link found below) for detailed information on how to apply for this scholarship.

title: Ertegun Graduate Scholarships in the Humanities at University of Oxford
description:
The Mica and Ahmet Ertegun Graduate Scholarship Programme funds full-time graduate study in the humanities at the University of Oxford. It aims to choose the very best students who will go on to become leaders in their fields. The scholarships are highly competitive, with over 1,500 applicants for around 15 awards each year.
The scholarship covers course fees in full and pays a grant for living costs (£21,805 a year in 2026-27), which is normally enough for a single student living in Oxford. Scholars also get dedicated use of Ertegun House for study and research, along with lectures, performances and social events. The award runs for the full length of the course and is renewed each year on satisfactory progress.
eligibility_text:
Students from all countries and all backgrounds, including UK students
The scholarship is for students starting a new full-time graduate course at Oxford. You must meet your course’s entry requirements, including English language requirements. The scholarship cannot be held with any other award, and current graduate students cannot apply for funding for their current course.
When you apply for your course on Oxford’s graduate application form, select “Ertegun Graduate Scholarships in the Humanities” in the funding section and upload the Ertegun supporting statement (three questions about the programme’s aims) as a PDF. Submit everything by Oxford’s early January deadline, which is 12 noon UK time on 5 January 2027 for most humanities courses. The listed Area Studies courses have different deadlines, so check your course page. Shortlisted candidates are interviewed by video or phone. First offers are expected by the end of March 2027 and the rest in April. It is important to visit the official website (link found below) for detailed information on how to apply for this scholarship.

title: University of the People Online Tuition Free Degrees
description:
University of the People (UoPeople) is a non-profit, fully online American university that does not charge tuition. Students pay a one-time application fee and an assessment fee for each course they take, and students who cannot afford these fees can ask for a need-based scholarship. All courses are online with no live lectures, so students study from home, and the university has students from more than 200 countries and territories. UoPeople is accredited by the WASC Senior College and University Commission (WSCUC).
There is no tuition. Students pay: •  a one-time, non-refundable application fee of US$60; •  an assessment fee for each course: US$180 for undergraduate courses, US$430 for M.Ed. courses and US$490 for MBA and MSIT courses. UoPeople estimates the total cost at about US$3,660 for an associate degree, US$7,080 to US$7,260 for a bachelor’s degree in business, computer science or health science, US$5,650 for the M.Ed. and US$5,940 for the MBA or MSIT. eligibility_text:
Students from any country
Applicants should: •  have finished secondary (high) school for an associate or bachelor’s degree, or hold a bachelor’s degree for a master’s degree; •  have good enough English to study at university level; •  have access to a computer and the internet. All new students first complete the UoPeople Foundations courses. Scholarships are need-based and only for admitted students; the general UoPeople scholarship is for associate and bachelor’s students who do not already have a university degree.
Apply online on the University of the People website and pay the application fee. There are five terms a year. The next application deadlines are 7 January 2027 for the term starting 28 January 2027 (early admissions deadline 17 December 2026) and 18 March 2027 for the term starting 8 April 2027 (early admissions deadline 25 February 2027). Once admitted, ask for a scholarship through the Financial Aid Office in the student portal; awards depend on financial need and the funds available, so apply as early as you can. title: Swedish Institute Scholarships for Global Professionals
description:
The Swedish Institute Scholarship for Global Professionals (SISGP) is a fully funded scholarship for Master’s studies in Sweden. It aims to develop future global leaders who will contribute to the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and to positive, sustainable development in their home countries and regions. Scholars also join the SI Network for Global Professionals.
•  full tuition fees •  living expenses of SEK 12,000 a month •  a one-time travel grant of SEK 15,000 (for scholars living outside Sweden) •  insurance •  membership of the SI Network for Global Professionals There are no extra grants for family members, and the University Admissions application fee is not covered.
eligibility_text:
Citizens of these 34 countries (you do not have to live there when you apply): Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bangladesh, Belarus, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Egypt, Ethiopia, Georgia, Guatemala, Indonesia, Iraq, Jordan, Kenya, Liberia, Malaysia, Mexico, Moldova, Morocco, Nigeria, Peru, Philippines, Rwanda, Senegal, South Africa, Tanzania, Thailand, Uganda, Ukraine, Uzbekistan, Vietnam and Zambia.
You must: •  be a citizen of one of the 34 eligible countries; •  apply for an SI-eligible Master’s programme and be liable to pay tuition fees; •  have work experience (applicants from most countries need at least 3,000 hours before February 2027); •  have leadership experience from an employer, entrepreneurship or civil society. You are not eligible if you are studying at or hold a degree from a Swedish university, have lived in Sweden for two years or more in total, or have already had an SI scholarship for studies in Sweden.
First apply for your Master’s programme(s) at universityadmissions.se between 16 October 2026 and 15 January 2027 . Then submit your SI scholarship application in the SI portal between 8 and 24 February 2027 (closes 14:59 CET). Admission results come out on 1 April 2027, and scholarship recipients are announced on 22 April 2027. It is important to visit the official website (link found below) for detailed information on how to apply for this scholarship.

title: American University Emerging Global Leader Scholarship
description:
The AU Emerging Global Leader Scholarship (AU EGLS) supports high-achieving international students who are dedicated to positive civic and social change and to improving under-resourced, underserved communities in their home country. It promotes access to education while adding to the international diversity of American University.
The full scholarship covers all billable AU expenses (full tuition, room and board). It does not cover non-billable costs such as health insurance, books, flights, taxes and personal expenses (about US$4,000 a year). The partial scholarships are worth up to US$40,000 a year. All awards are renewable for four years of undergraduate study with good academic performance.
eligibility_text:
International students who need a non-immigrant (F-1 or J-1) visa to study in the US
Preference is given to: •  students who have overcome obstacles, and those from diverse and underrepresented global and socioeconomic backgrounds; •  students with a commitment to leadership, volunteering, community service and the needs of people in their home country; •  students who meet AU’s English requirements; •  students still in secondary school and graduating by June 2027. US citizens, US permanent residents and dual US citizens cannot apply. Applicants must show at least US$4,000 a year on the AU Declaration of Finances Form and a bank letter.
First submit the Common Application with all supporting documents and official English test scores, then submit the AU EGLS application and essays through your applicant portal. Both must be done by 15 January 2027 ; Regular Decision is recommended. Finalists are interviewed, and winners are notified by 1 April 2027. Applicants who are not selected can still be considered for admission and partial merit scholarships. It is important to visit the official website (link found below) for detailed information on how to apply for this scholarship.
